$comment: Machine-readable record of every field test: a build in a hand, on a real device, against the live relay. This exists because the defects that reach this stage are the ones no test and no CI run can see — a ViewModel recreated by Android, a location provider that answers fast and coarse, an EXIF block that is simply absent. Each entry is what was OBSERVED, kept separate from what was CONCLUDED: `timeline` and `report` are transcribed from client_events and D1 and must never be edited to fit a later understanding, while `findings` is interpretation and may be revised. Written after the fact from the relay's own records, so a test that produced nothing to read produces no entry. A `docs/research/` write-up of a test should cite the id here, and so should a decision a test caused; none does yet, because no test has produced one yet.
source: D1 tables client_events and reports on the live relay, plus Cloudflare Workers Logs
notes: Timelines are transcribed verbatim, including the events that record a mistake. A tester who changed their mind produced two category-chosen events; both stay. Trimming a timeline to the happy path destroys the only evidence of what the interaction actually felt like.

atMs is milliseconds since the telemetry session began, which is the app process starting. It is the only ordering that survives, because the relay stamps received_at at flush time rather than at the moment of the event. That column is still worth reading: every event of one batch shares its value, so a batch boundary is legible, a flush is datable, and a batch that never arrived leaves a hole with a shape. Grouping one session by received_at is how #74 was found, and an earlier version of this note claimed the opposite.
A session id is random per process, never persisted, and cannot follow anyone between sessions (data/relay-events.json). Recording it here links a timeline to its report and to nothing else.
dryRun records whether the relay was armed. A test against an unarmed relay proves the app and the relay and says nothing about the city.

A screenshot is not in this repository and never will be. The five that came back across the first iOS field test, from both testers together, are photographs of two volunteers' homes; the repository is public and MIT. Where a screenshot is the only source for a finding, the entry says so and the finding stands on that alone.

tests.what: First run of the Android app on real hardware against the live relay: the whole walk from camera to a recorded report, twice, by the developer indoors.

device.note: The developer's own phone, sideloaded over adb. Not a tester device.

build.signingNote: Android has no release signing chain yet (#58); the parity manifest records signed-release as ios-only. A release VARIANT was required regardless, because the relay host is a buildConfigField and only the release variant carries the deployed one.
build.hostVerifiedOn: the artifact, not the build log: classes.dex contains the deployed host and contains no loopback literal

relay.note: Unarmed throughout. Nothing in this test could reach the city, which is why it was safe to run and why it says nothing about the city's behaviour.

report.municipalityCheck: passed; the coordinate reverse-looked to SVFNR 0000, Reykjavíkurborg
report.descriptionShape: the typed text, then a blank line, then the relay's appended nearest registered address

server.note: No exception, no warning, no rejection anywhere in Workers Logs for the window.

confirmed.claim: A photo the app captures itself carries no EXIF GPS, so the device fix is the primary source on the capture path rather than the fallback.
confirmed.evidence: location-failed {reason: no-exif} preceded the device fix on both captures, at elapsedMs 1 and 0.
confirmed.wherePredicted: AGENTS.md, from CameraX's documented behaviour; docs/research/photos-exif-and-formats.md
confirmed.note: First observation of this on real Android hardware. It had been reasoned about, not measured.

confirmed.claim: The whole chain works end to end from a phone: camera, coordinate, category, relay, D1.
confirmed.evidence: send-result 201 in 1390 ms, and a matching row in reports.

confirmed.claim: A 2.29 MB JPEG passes the relay's size and magic-byte gates.
confirmed.evidence: photoBytes 2290923 recorded, no rejection. The city's stated limit is 8 MB.

findings.what: app-opened fired twice in one session, 16 minutes apart, because it was emitted from PocViewModel's init and a ViewModel is Activity-scoped while the telemetry session is process-scoped.
findings.evidence: atMs 1 and atMs 955703, same session id, therefore the same process.
findings.whyOnlyHere: No unit test can observe an Activity being recreated, and CI cannot background an app. It needed a phone in a hand for sixteen minutes.
findings.consequence: app-opened is the denominator of every funnel this channel exists to support, so completion rates read lower than they are.
findings.status: fixed; emitted from BorgarlandApplication.onCreate, which runs once per process, guarded by AppOpenedOncePerProcessTest

findings.what: The device fix supplies the coordinate, its accuracy is measured, and nothing gates or stores it. DeviceFix.liveFix races every enabled provider and takes whichever answers first; usable() checks only that the numbers are finite.
findings.evidence: Two fixes in one session, 14 m and 51 m, both resolving in about 240 ms, which is a network or cached fix rather than GPS. The 51 m one is the coordinate on the submitted report.
findings.consequence: The reports table has no accuracy column, so nothing downstream can tell a good fix from a poor one. The relay then appends a specific house number derived from it, and the address sentence is more precise than the coordinate that produced it.
findings.correctedInIssue: #31's body claimed DeviceFix already reasons about accuracy on the device path. It does not.
findings.status: recorded on #31; no code change

notFoundHere: Nothing about the city. The relay was unarmed, so the adapter, the city's validator and the reference-number parse were all untouched by this test (#56).
Nothing about a poor network. Both sends ran on wifi indoors; a 1390 ms send says little about the same walk on mobile data at the edge of coverage.
Nothing about the gallery path, which does not exist on either platform (#28). Every EXIF question this project has is a gallery-path question, and this test could not reach it.
Nothing about a cold outdoor GPS fix. Both fixes came from indoors in seconds, which is the case where the provider race resolves coarse.

tests.what: Verification of the #70 fix on the same phone that found it: the Activity destroyed and recreated three times inside one process, which is the exact condition that produced the duplicate.

build.hostVerifiedOn: the artifact: BorgarlandApplication is present in classes.dex, so Android had a class to instantiate

relay.note: Unarmed. No report was created; this test never left the camera screen.

tests.method: adb: force-stop for a fresh process, then launch, KEYCODE_BACK, launch, KEYCODE_BACK, launch, KEYCODE_HOME. Back finishes the Activity and clears the ViewModel while the process stays warm, which is what the first walk hit by hand. onStop flushes the buffer.

confirmed.claim: app-opened now fires once per process, whatever the Activity does.
confirmed.evidence: Three Activity creations in one session produced three camera-permission events and exactly one app-opened. The process id was unchanged throughout and the session id was unchanged, so this is one process.
confirmed.note: On the old code the same sequence would have produced three. The first walk produced two by accident; this produced one on purpose.

confirmed.claim: The manifest registration works, so the Application is actually instantiated.
confirmed.evidence: An app-opened event exists at all. An Application class Android is not told about is never constructed, and the event would simply have gone missing.

findings.what: camera-permission fires once per Activity creation, so it appeared three times in this session.
findings.whyNotADefect: It reports a state rather than a decision, and it is nobody's denominator: a session where the permission was granted is still countable as one. It is redundant rather than misleading, which is the difference from app-opened.
findings.status: recorded, not filed

notFoundHere: Nothing about a rotation, which is the other way Android recreates an Activity. Back was used because it is scriptable over adb; the lifetime argument is the same either way.
Nothing about a process death and restore, where Android recreates the Activity after killing the process. That produces a NEW session, and a new app-opened is then correct.
Nothing about the rest of the walk. This session never captured a photo, so it says nothing about location, the category picker or a send.

tests.what: The first run of the app by somebody who did not build it: a volunteer tester in Seattle, on TestFlight, guided step by step over Messenger. Being 5,630 km from the nearest Icelandic address he could exercise everything up to the municipality check and nothing past it, which makes him the only person who has met the refusal path on a real phone.

device.note: The telemetry channel carries no device identifier of any kind, by design (data/relay-events.json), and nothing else in this test recorded one. Nobody's phone model is known here and that is the intended cost. His device clock was on Pacific time, which distorts nothing here: atMs is elapsed milliseconds since the process started, and received_at is stamped by the relay.

build.signing: Apple team B4724Z74TM, the party's team; the certificate and the API key are team-scoped, so nothing app-specific was created for this
build.hostVerifiedOn: the events themselves. A release build carries one host and only one since #51, so an event arriving at the deployed relay is proof the build was not pointing at the loopback.

relay.note: Unarmed throughout, and confirmed unarmed afterwards from /api/health. Nothing either tester did could reach the city, which is why it was safe to put the app in a stranger's hands at all, and why neither test says anything about the city's behaviour.

tests.method: Guided over Messenger by the developer, who could not see the screen. Every observation below is either in D1 or in a screenshot the tester sent; nothing here is a memory of what somebody said happened.
tests.deliveryNote: Every event of one batch shares received_at, so a batch boundary is legible in that column and a flush is datable. Solving for the session start from the second batch puts it at 20:13:10.7Z; the third gives 20:13:17.6Z, and the seven seconds between them are the flush latency the method cannot see past. Either way the first batch is a flush that happened more than two minutes after its last event, which is the app being backgrounded rather than a threshold being reached.
tests.storedRow: none. outside-reykjavik is thrown by the jurisdiction check before insertReport, so a refused report leaves nothing behind at all, and the reports table holds no row for this session.

confirmed.claim: The municipality check refuses a coordinate outside Reykjavík, and refuses it before storing anything.
confirmed.evidence: send-result {status: 400, ok: false} at atMs 192375, and no row in reports for this session, while the Reykjavík session the same evening produced two.
confirmed.wherePredicted: AGENTS.md: the city validates nothing, not even that a coordinate exists, so the relay has to.

confirmed.claim: A photo the app captures itself carries no EXIF GPS on iOS either, so the device fix is the primary source on the capture path rather than the fallback.
confirmed.evidence: location-failed {reason: no-exif} preceded every fix, at elapsedMs 14 and 1.
confirmed.wherePredicted: docs/research/photos-exif-and-formats.md, established on Android and on Biggi's uncompressed original
confirmed.note: First observation of this on iOS hardware. It had been reasoned about from the API, not measured.

confirmed.claim: The whole chain runs from a stranger's phone: TestFlight build, camera, device fix, category, relay, D1.
confirmed.evidence: Twenty events across three batches, and a relay answer in 2209 ms.

findings.what: The registry's nearest-address scan has no distance bound, so every point on Earth resolves to an Icelandic address and the answer never says how far away nearest was.
findings.evidence: The refusal named Sauðanesviti, 431 Suðureyri as the nearest address to a coordinate in Seattle. Great-circle to the registry's own row for it: 5,630 km.
findings.whyOnlyHere: No test had ever put a coordinate outside Iceland through the check, because nobody working on it had been outside Iceland.
findings.consequence: The Seattle direction is benign, since it fails anyway. The mirror case is not: a coordinate whose nearest address happens to carry SVFNR 0000 passes however far away it is.
findings.status: open

findings.what: The refusal was shown to him as the relay's raw JSON, with no sentence saying what had happened.
findings.evidence: He read {"error":"outside-reykjavik",...,"nearestAddress":"Sauðanesviti, 431 Suðureyri","svfnr":4200} off the screen and asked what it meant.
findings.whyOnlyHere: Everyone who had used the app until this evening had written the relay, and read that body as a diagnostic rather than as a message.
findings.status: fixed in #84; every relay outcome is now one sentence from data/relay-outcomes.json, with the raw body behind a control

findings.what: The app told him the location permission was missing 37 ms after the photograph, while the system dialog asking for it was still on his screen.
findings.evidence: location-permission {granted: false} at atMs 14127, elapsedMs 37 from the capture, then granted: true at 30108 once he had answered.
findings.whyOnlyHere: The developers' phones had granted the permission long ago, so the first-launch path had never run on a device that had not already answered it.
findings.consequence: Every first-time user emits a spurious denial, which is the exact event this channel exists to count.
findings.status: open

notFoundHere: Nothing about the city. The relay was in dry run and forwarded nothing, so this test proves the app and the relay and stops there.
Nothing about the gallery path, which does not exist on either platform (data/platform-parity.json records gallery-pick as neither-yet).
Nothing about a Reykjavík coordinate. He never reached the far side of the municipality check, so everything past it is untested by this entry.
No device model, no crash data and no screen recording. The channel is deliberately incapable of carrying the first, and nothing crashed.

tests.what: The second volunteer, in Reykjavík, on the same TestFlight build. He completed the walk end to end and then ran three deliberate tests on purpose: sending in airplane mode, taking a photo with the location permission turned off in Settings, and the category picker. Six of the seven issues from that night come from this session.

device.note: The telemetry channel carries no device identifier of any kind, by design (data/relay-events.json), and nothing else in this test recorded one. Nobody's phone model is known here and that is the intended cost.

build.signing: Apple team B4724Z74TM, the party's team; the certificate and the API key are team-scoped, so nothing app-specific was created for this
build.hostVerifiedOn: the events themselves. A release build carries one host and only one since #51, so an event arriving at the deployed relay is proof the build was not pointing at the loopback.

relay.note: Unarmed throughout, and confirmed unarmed afterwards from /api/health. Nothing either tester did could reach the city, which is why it was safe to put the app in a stranger's hands at all, and why neither test says anything about the city's behaviour.

tests.method: Guided over Messenger by the developer, who could not see the screen. Screenshots came back and are NOT in this repository: they are photographs of a volunteer's home. Five came back across the whole test, from both testers together, and this entry claims no count of its own. Every observation below that a screenshot is the only source for says so.
tests.deliveryNote: Every event of one batch shares received_at, so a batch boundary is legible in that column. That is not a detail: the fourth batch is a single send-failed arriving alone, with no send-started before it, and noticing that is how #74 was found.

timelineHole.whatIsMissing: A category was chosen, a description of 22 characters was typed, the details screen was left and a send was started. None of it is in D1.
timelineHole.howWeKnow: send-failed at 603005 carries elapsedMs 84101, so its send started at 518904, and a send cannot run without a category (selectedSlug). The description is legible in the tester's screenshot while the last length D1 holds is 0.
timelineHole.why: A flush fired while the phone was in airplane mode, took the buffer, failed, and discarded it (#74). The flush point was the app being backgrounded, which is what reaching the Control Center to toggle airplane mode does.
timelineHole.readingRule: This gap is indistinguishable from a person standing still for two and a half minutes. It is recorded here because the timeline itself cannot say which it was, and a future reader must not count it as idle time.

reports.note: The same report as the row above, filed a second time 35 seconds later. Same category, and a photo byte count matching the FIRST of the session's three photo-captured events, at atMs 27511; the other two, at 427065 and 631650, carry different counts and neither was ever sent (#85).

confirmed.claim: The whole walk works end to end from a stranger's phone in Reykjavík: camera, device fix, category, description, relay, a stored row.
confirmed.evidence: send-result {status: 201, ok: true} in 3611 ms at atMs 74182, and a matching row created at 20:20:20.554Z.

confirmed.claim: A Reykjavík coordinate passes the municipality check, which is the half of it the Seattle test could not reach.
confirmed.evidence: Both stored rows exist, and the relay stores nothing that fails the check.

confirmed.claim: The device fix answers fast and coarse indoors, exactly as it does on Android.
confirmed.evidence: accuracyM 7 twice, resolving in 7046 ms on the first attempt and 22 ms on the second, which is a cached or network fix rather than GPS.
confirmed.wherePredicted: the Android field test, 2026-08-23-android-first-walk, which saw 14 m and 51 m in about 240 ms
confirmed.note: Still nothing gates or stores the accuracy: #31.

findings.what: The telemetry buffer was emptied before the request and the flush was fire-and-forget, so a flush into airplane mode discarded its events.
findings.evidence: A 161-second hole between atMs 441749 and 603005, and a send-failed arriving alone in its own batch with no send-started before it.
findings.whyOnlyHere: No unit test and no CI run can put a phone in airplane mode between two events. The hole is only visible by grouping the events of one session by their delivery.
findings.consequence: The instrument loses data exactly while the failure it exists to measure is happening, so every offline defect is under-reported by construction.
findings.status: fixed in #80; a batch the relay did not take goes back in the buffer, on both platforms

findings.what: The send lost the network and lost the report with it, and the wait was not bounded by the timeout in the code.
findings.evidence: send-failed {elapsedMs: 84101, reason: timeout} while RelayClient set a 30-second timeoutInterval. He restored the network about thirty seconds in and it failed anyway.
findings.whyOnlyHere: timeoutInterval is an idle timeout that restarts when the network changes; nothing but a real network change reveals that, and no test had ever produced one.
findings.consequence: He left the screen through Byrja aftur, which abandons the report rather than cancelling the request, because it was the only live control on the screen.
findings.status: fixed in #81; the report is written to the phone before the attempt, the whole operation is bounded, and the send control offers a way out

findings.what: With the permission turned off in Settings, Reyna aftur could only ever return the same refusal, and nothing on the screen opened Settings.
findings.evidence: location-permission {granted: false} at atMs 631734 and again at 641821 after he pressed it, ten seconds apart, the second one returning the same answer.
findings.whyOnlyHere: It needs a permission that has been denied at the system level, which a developer's own phone almost never has.
findings.status: fixed in #83; a denial that will not be revisited is told apart from one that has not been answered, and offers Opna stillingar

findings.what: The successful send was shown to him as the relay's whole stored row plus the whole cityPayload, with no sentence saying it had worked.
findings.evidence: He asked whether the app was connected to anything at all. The 201 body carries sentAt, accepted, cityStatus, cityReference, rejection, outcome and outcomeAt, which is the follow-through machinery of #56 and #57.
findings.consequence: He pressed send again 31 seconds later and filed the same ábending twice (#85).
findings.status: fixed in #84; the screen leads with one sentence and the raw body is behind a control

findings.what: After a report is accepted the send button returns to its unsent state, fully live, as though nothing had been sent.
findings.evidence: Two stored rows 35 seconds apart, both carrying the byte count of the same photograph, the one captured at atMs 27511; send-started at 70570 and again at 105431, with no retry path in the app at the time, so nothing but a person could have begun the second.
findings.whyOnlyHere: Everyone who had used the app knew what a 201 meant, so nobody had ever pressed the button twice.
findings.consequence: In dry run it costs a duplicate row. Once the relay is armed the same press files a second ábending into a real work queue.
findings.status: open

findings.what: The app told him the location permission was missing 118 ms after the photograph, while the system dialog asking for it was still on his screen.
findings.evidence: location-permission {granted: false} at atMs 27629, elapsedMs 118 from the capture, then granted: true at 34528 once he had answered. The genuine denials in this same session, at 631734 and 641821, are a different situation.
findings.consequence: Every first-time user emits a spurious denial, which is the exact event this channel exists to count.
findings.status: open

findings.what: The details screen scrolls under the status bar, so the system clock is drawn on top of a category name.
findings.evidence: A screenshot, which is the only source: nothing about layout can reach this channel. In it, 8:26 sits on top of Ruslafötur and both are unreadable.
findings.status: open

findings.what: Once the description keyboard is up there is no way to put it away.
findings.evidence: The tester's own words, over Messenger: "Enginn augljós leið til að loka þessu, og fjarlægja lyklaborðið." No timeline event can carry this.
findings.consequence: The description is the last field in the flow that asks anyone to type, so everyone who files a report meets it.
findings.status: open

notFoundHere: Nothing about the city. The relay was in dry run and forwarded nothing.
Nothing about what the offline walk actually looked like as an interaction. The events that would have said were discarded by the bug this test found, and the fix arrived after the test.
No confirmation that telemetry survives an outage. It did not, and the entry above records the opposite; the fix in #80 is unverified on a device.
Nothing about the gallery path or a map, neither of which exists.
No second opinion on the layout findings. #78 and #79 rest on one screenshot and one sentence from one person, on one device.

tests.what: The Android walk run twice on a phone after the nine field-test fixes merged: once end to end to a recorded report, once to meet a denied location permission and come back from it. This is the run #101 was filed about, transcribed from D1 a day later.

device.note: The telemetry channel carries no device identifier by design (data/relay-events.json), and app_version is 0.1.0 (1) on every Android build so far, so it cannot tell one phone from another. The session handoff written that night says SM-A715F, the SMS-gateway A71. That is the only source, it is a memory rather than a measurement, and it is recorded here as such. The developer's SM-S918B also had the app installed at the time, so the two are not distinguishable from anything in this file.

build.signingNote: Android still has no release signing chain (#58); a release VARIANT is required regardless, because the relay host is a buildConfigField and only release carries the deployed one.
build.hostVerifiedOn: the events themselves: they arrived at the deployed relay, which a loopback build could not have reached.

relay.note: Unarmed throughout. The relay was on version 01703e95, deployed 23:46:15Z, 97 seconds before the first event of this session. It still had the counted live gate later replaced by #98, which is irrelevant here because dry run never reaches that branch. Corrected 2026-08-24: this said d31a0d99, which was the version 23 hours earlier and was copied from #56's 'Ready as of 2026-08-23 00:45' note rather than read off the deployments ledger.

tests.method: Transcribed from D1 on 2026-08-24 by querying client_events and reports directly, not from the chat transcript or the PR bodies that were the only record for a day.
tests.deliveryNote: Two batches. The first carries the app-opened pair; the second carries everything from the photograph to the send, flushed after the report came back. The 51-second gap between them is the tester composing, not a hole.

reports.municipalityCheck: passed; the coordinate reverse-looked to a Reykjavík address
reports.descriptionShape: the typed text, then a blank line, then the relay's appended nearest registered address: Gullengi 39, 112 Reykjavík

confirmed.claim: The whole walk works on hardware against the deployed relay: camera, device fix, category, description, send, row in D1.
confirmed.evidence: send-result 201 in 466 ms at atMs 124504, and report 069fe188779f2e7d3ac42436e0985c48 created_at 23:49:56.121Z — 210 ms before that event's batch reached the relay at 23:49:56.331Z. The row precedes the event because the relay writes it while answering the send; the two clocks are D1's and the relay's, both server-side.

confirmed.claim: A photo the app captures itself still carries no EXIF GPS, so the device fix is the primary source on the capture path.
confirmed.evidence: location-failed {reason: no-exif} at atMs 50981, before location-resolved {source: device} at 51301.
confirmed.note: Third independent observation of this on Android hardware.

confirmed.claim: A denied location permission no longer dead-ends the walk, and granting it in Settings resumes the walk without a restart (#76).
confirmed.evidence: session 444fa4780aaf67c94efa2dedfa5c5b9a: location-permission {granted: false} at atMs 7526 with location-failed {reason: permission} in the same millisecond, then location-permission {granted: true} at 47282 and location-resolved at 47288 — 40 seconds later, in the SAME session, so the same process. The screen waited rather than failing.

notFoundHere: Nothing about the city. The relay was unarmed, so the adapter, the city's validator and the reference-number parse were untouched (#56).

Nothing about WHICH phone this was. The channel carries no device identifier and that is the intended privacy cost; the handoff's SM-A715F is a memory, and this file does not launder it into a measurement.

Nothing about the reworded category label (#40). The walk chose ruslafotur and category-chosen carries a slug, never a label, so no event here can show what any screen said. The 2026-08-24 entry is the first that can.
Nothing about the offline queue, which is iOS-only (data/platform-parity.json) and which Android therefore still lacks.
Nothing about a report id on the wire. This build predates #95 on Android; the id in the row above was generated by the relay.

tests.what: Two walks in one session on the developer's own phone, on a build of main made minutes earlier. The first verified the #110 keyboard fix and was driven over adb; the second was walked by hand by Guðröður through almenn-abending, which is the first time anyone has recorded reaching the reworded label on a screen.

device.note: Established, unlike the entry above: the phone was attached over adb throughout and `adb shell getprop ro.product.model` answered. Sideloaded, not a tester device.

build.signingNote: Signed by hand with ~/.android/debug.keystore after zipalign, because #58 is still open. Installed 2026-08-24 03:47:40, confirmed with `adb shell dumpsys package`.
build.hostVerifiedOn: the events themselves, which arrived at the deployed relay.

relay.note: Version bdadab48, deployed 03:24:08Z. The SECOND carrying the #98 reorder, not the first: #105 shipped in d8ca63ae at 02:24:09Z and bdadab48 an hour later added #108. Confirmed unarmed after the deploy: `wrangler secret list` returned [] and rows with dry_run = 0 numbered 0.

tests.method: The first walk was driven over adb with uiautomator locating every control; the second was performed by hand. Transcribed from D1, not from the driver's own logs.
tests.deliveryNote: Two batches, one per walk. The 16-minute gap between them is the phone sitting idle between the adb-driven walk and the hand-walked one, in the same process.

confirmed.claim: The #110 keyboard fix works: with the IME shown, the submit control is reachable, where before it was absent from the accessibility tree at any scroll position.
confirmed.evidence: Measured with `dumpsys input_method` and `uiautomator dump`, same two commands before and after the fix. Before: mInputShown=true, Áfram absent, bottom-most node y=1789. After: mInputShown=true, bottom-most node y=2316, and one scroll puts Áfram at y=1240, above the keyboard. Screen height 2316.
confirmed.note: Not visible in this timeline: the walk's events look identical either way. The measurement is the record, which is why it is written here rather than inferred from atMs.

confirmed.claim: The reworded label reaches a screen. Both pickers were only ever verified by grepping data/category-labels.json; this is the first time anyone has recorded seeing it.
confirmed.evidence: The picker rendered 'Annað í almannarými' with its help line 'Bekkur, girðing, tré eða annað sem á ekki heima í hinum flokkunum.', read verbatim off the device with `uiautomator dump` and matching data/category-labels.json byte for byte. Then category-chosen {slug: almenn-abending} at atMs 1104139, walked by hand, producing report d234a2712fa073652b75145461fb0a11.
confirmed.note: AGENTS.md said for a day that no build anyone was holding showed this. That stops being true here.

confirmed.claim: The relay's answer reaches the person as a sentence rather than as JSON, and the send button reads Sent and is disabled afterwards.
confirmed.evidence: Observed on the confirm screen after the first walk: the button greyed out reading 'Sent', above 'Þjónustan tók við ábendingunni en sendi hana ekki áfram. Hún er í þurrkeyrslu, svo ekkert fór til borgarinnar. Þetta var æfing.' — the outcome sentence from data/relay-outcomes.json.
confirmed.note: Neither had any evidence anywhere that it reached a screen. Like the label, they were verified by reading the file that supplies them.

confirmed.claim: The device fix accuracy varies by an order of magnitude between two captures minutes apart, and nothing gates on it.
confirmed.evidence: location-resolved accuracyM 49 at atMs 6172 and accuracyM 5 at 1094093, both source device, both accepted without comment. The 49 m fix is the coordinate on the first report.
confirmed.wherePredicted: #31, which is open and says exactly this

findings.what: The soft keyboard covered the Áfram button and the content could not scroll past it, leaving a field of empty background where the button should be, so the screen read as finished.
findings.evidence: With the IME shown the accessibility tree ended at y=1789 on a 2316-tall screen and contained no Áfram node at any scroll position.

findings.what: category-chosen's elapsedMs is measured from PHOTO CAPTURE, not from reaching the category screen, so it includes the whole location step. Two issues and one correction read it as time spent choosing a category.
findings.evidence: Across all nine entries elapsedMs equals category-chosen.atMs minus photo-captured.atMs to within 1 ms. Here it is 108399 ms while only 8132 ms passed between location-resolved and category-chosen: she spent 100 seconds on a permission she had refused, and the metric counted it as picking a category. data/relay-events.json declares the field as 'integer' and says nothing about what it is elapsed from.
findings.whyNotADefect: The number is not wrong, the reading of it was. Recomputed as time from location-resolved to category-chosen, the two known first-time users are 8.1 s (her, iOS) and 8.3 s (Guðmundur, Android). The 29.8 s that #115 was filed about stands alone as one session, not a platform and not a familiarity effect. Both the issue's original hypothesis and the correction written earlier today are unsupported.
findings.status: open in #115, with the metric definition now the actual finding
